definitions.explanation: Gaining control over a region, field, or rivals so as to stand above all others. Takes する to mean to dominate or conquer.

definitions.gloss: winning a title; taking the championship
definitions.explanation: In sports and competition, winning a tournament or title outright — beating all comers to the top. {全国|ぜんこく}{制覇|せいは} is a set phrase for winning a national championship.

examples.japanese: {世界|せかい}{制覇|せいは}をたくらむ。
その{企業|きぎょう}は{国内|こくない}{市場|しじょう}を{制覇|せいは}した。
examples.english: That company dominated the domestic market.

examples.japanese: {戦国|せんごく}{時代|じだい}、{天下|てんか}{制覇|せいは}を{目指|めざ}した{武将|ぶしょう}は{数多|かずおお}くいた。
examples.english: In the Warring States period, there were many warlords who aimed to conquer the whole country.

examples.japanese: {全国|ぜんこく}{制覇|せいは}を{果|は}たした。
{悲願|ひがん}の{全国|ぜんこく}{制覇|せいは}を{目指|めざ}して{練習|れんしゅう}している。
examples.english: They are training in pursuit of the national title they have long dreamed of.

examples.japanese: {強豪|きょうごう}チームを{次々|つぎつぎ}と{破|やぶ}り、ついに{大会|たいかい}{制覇|せいは}を{成|な}し{遂|と}げた。
examples.english: Beating strong teams one after another, they finally achieved victory in the tournament.

notes:
Literally "to control and cover." The conquest sense (sense 1) covers markets, territory, and rivals; the sports sense (sense 2) is essentially winning a title, most often in the set phrase {全国|ぜんこく}{制覇|せいは}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {全国|ぜんこく}{制覇|せいは}: winning a national championship
- {世界|せかい}{制覇|せいは}: world domination
- {天下|てんか}{制覇|せいは}: conquering the realm
- {市場|しじょう}を{制覇|せいは}する: to dominate a market

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {征服|せいふく}: conquest/subjugation — emphasizes forcibly subduing, especially by military means
- {優勝|ゆうしょう}: winning a championship — the plain word for taking first place, without the nuance of dominating all rivals
